metadata.title: Microsoft and Amazon Lead Tech Spending Survey

content.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) and Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) screened well in a Jefferies survey showing stronger 2026 spending intentions for software, cloud and AI.
Jefferies surveyed 40 IT executives and found expected software budget growth of 6.2% in 2026, up from 4.8% in 2025. Cloud spending is expected to grow 10.1%, while cybersecurity budgets are projected to rise 6.2%. AI also remains a major priority, with 68% of CIOs now having dedicated AI budgets.
Microsoft stood out, with 85% of CIOs expecting to spend more in 2026 and none planning to spend less. AWS also screened positively, with 56% expecting higher spending. Palo Alto Networks (NASDAQ:PANW) and ServiceNow (NYSE:NOW) also ranked well, while Adobe (NASDAQ:ADBE) was the weak spot, with a negative spending score.
Jefferies said AI and security remain top priorities, and token and API spending is already running above plan for many companies.
